In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the trapping efficiency is very sensitive to the geometry of the fault zone structure.
fault zones with a width of a few kilometers and with moderate irregularities can be expected to produce trapped waves which are observable at the surface.

2-D models of fault zone structures can be used to interpret the generation of fault zone waves in the case of modestly irregular structures, but that 3-D effects may have to be taken into account when the fault zone structure becomes highly irregular.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the trapping efficiency of fault zones is not very sensitive to modest 3-D effects, while the trapping of energy in the fault zone is highly sensitive to the location of the source relative to the fault zone.
3-D effects in fault zones can be neglected for modeling purposes if the fault zone structure is known to a sufficient accuracy.
2-D models are adequate for most applications, and that the 3-D effects are modest for realistic fault zone structures.

the trapping of energy is very sensitive to the geometry of the fault zone structure, and thus accurate modeling of wave motion in fault zones may be a powerful tool for imaging the geometry of fault zones.
